analysis.title: GS Consumer | Morning Trading Update (US)
key_insights: US equities are better bid pre-market (SPX +25bps, NDX +45bps, RTY +30bps) on light news flow apart from Iran headlines (Iran's Supreme Leader reportedly called for meeting conditions to end the war). WTI is -80bps at $101, UST2yr -2.5bps at 4.69%, UST10yr -1.5bps at 4.975%, 30yr -1bp at 5.29%.
Focus is on tomorrow's FOMC and on megacap earnings: MSFT, GOOG, NOW and KLAC report tomorrow, AMZN and INTC on Thursday.

The AI trade is firmer after yesterday's rally: Tokyo Electron +3%, Hynix +5%, Samsung +4% in Asia, SMH +1% and DRAM +2.5% pre-market. AVGO is +2.4% pre-market and reportedly arranged a $63bn deal to finance the purchase of chips (Bloomberg).
Internationally, Novartis is +1.5% after results, while HSBC is -6%, Reckitt -4% and Mercedes -3%.

HLT is -5% pre-market on a weaker Q4 guide and long positioning going in. Q3 EPS was $2.45 ex-items vs $2.37 consensus, revenue $3.33B vs $3.37B consensus, RevPAR +5.8% vs +4.6% consensus aided by the World Cup and calendar shifts. Q4 EPS guide of $2.32-2.38 is below the $2.39 consensus on RevPAR of +3.0-3.5%, with midterms and the Middle East flagged as headwinds.

RCL is +5% on solid forward commentary. Q3 EPS was $6.57 vs $6.38 consensus. FY EPS guide was raised to $17.85-$17.95 (consensus $17.79). Q4 net yields are expected to inflect to the mid-4% range from +0.6% in Q3, 2027 bookings are pacing ahead of historical levels at higher rates, and management framed a $20 handle on 2027 EPS (consensus $20.32).

KO is -0.5% to -1% pre-market after a solid quarter, as the stock fades on full valuation. Q3 EPS was $0.91 vs $0.88 consensus, organic revenue +7% vs +4.4% consensus. North America was +3% vs +4% consensus, while LatAm was +16% vs +7% and Asia Pacific +6% vs -1%. FY EPS guide was raised by 150 bps and organic revenue guide is now at least +5%.

SMPL is -2% to -3%: Q4 beat but fiscal 2027 guidance is weak. Q1 sales guide is -19% to -22% (vs -12.2% consensus) and FY27 sales guide is -13% to -17% (vs -8.7% consensus). FY27 Adj. EBITDA guide is -9% to -14% (vs -2.0% consensus).
SFD is -2%: adjusted EPS was in line at $0.26 but sales missed ($3.44bn vs $3.69bn estimate), led by pork and packaged meats. Management expects total sales down low-single digits from fiscal 2025.

WHR is -8% on a large miss and another guidance cut. Q3 EPS was -$0.21 ex-items vs $0.73 consensus, and the FY adj. EPS outlook was cut to -$1.30 vs $1.21 consensus. Freight and raw material costs are offsetting pricing and productivity gains, and a 7+% price increase in North America and Latin America MDA takes effect in December.

SHW is -4% to -5% on a Q3 EPS miss ($3.63 vs $3.69 consensus) despite sales ahead ($6.86bn vs $6.78bn). Paint Stores and Consumer Brands segment profit missed. The FY guide was narrowed around the same midpoint ($11.85-12.15). The options market implies a 2% move on the call.

PII is up 3-7% on a large beat helped by tariff refunds. Q3 EPS was $1.08 ex-items vs $0.59 consensus, including $0.13 of tariff refunds. The FY EPS guide was raised to $3.50-3.60 (vs $3.14 consensus), with about $1.09 attributed to tariff refunds, and this is the third guidance raise this year.
ONON is -4% after Chinese brands (Dongpeng, Mengniu, Milkground) cut ties with Kylian Mbappé over remarks apparently calling Mao Zedong a dictator.

GM is +3% after announcing a move of its listing from the NYSE to the Nasdaq Global Select Market effective Nov. 17, keeping the GM ticker. The move creates potential Nasdaq-100 inclusion eligibility and passive index demand.

GS Research reiterates Buy on PM after a strong Q3 and keeps it a top stock idea. Catalysts are ZYN innovation (20 pouches), the US launch of ILUMA, a next-generation IQOS in 1H27 and a buyback reauthorization. The stock is at a ~10% discount to growth staples peers.
GS sees DG metrics still strong but moderating ahead of 3Q. DG trades at 16.1x P/E. GS expects continued top-line momentum from higher fuel prices and stays cautious on FY27 margin expansion.
GS sees mixed price and value trends at BJ ahead of 3Q. Net purchase intent is improving, but the stock trades at 21.5x P/E vs a 1-year average of 19.8x.

The GS Housing Activity Scale fell to 3 from 4, the lowest reading since the pandemic, down 3% sequentially and 11% y/y. Purchase applications fell 7% and sales fell 3%, while the mortgage rate fell 8bps to 7.32%. GS highlights IBP (buy), MTH and DHI.

GS expects TKO Q3 revenue slightly above consensus ($1,387M vs $1,376M) and adjusted EBITDA below ($537M vs $556M) on weaker WWE results. It keeps Buy and lowers the PT to $215 from $220. For Liberty Formula One it keeps Buy and lowers the PT to $116 from $117.
Citi upgraded FERG.

MSFT, GOOG, NOW and KLAC report on 2026-10-28. AMZN and INTC report on 2026-10-29.
